positions.why: It beat and raised on every line (EPS $1.89 vs $1.66, organic growth guide 8-9%, $289B backlog), closed $2 under its 52-week high with low 3.3% weekly volatility, gains from the Iran conflict, and has no report this week.

Healthcare is where the rotation money is going, and JNJ has the strongest large-cap chart: +4.1% follow-through, 2% below its 52-week high, a negative sector correlation to SPY and no report this week.
The bank that benefits from rising rates sits at an all-time high with low 2.2% weekly volatility, the 10Y-2Y spread has widened to +34 bps, and the banks have finished reporting.

It is the book's only tech position and its hedge against a tech rebound: it doesn't report until Aug 26, trades at about 16x forward earnings, is up 7% in four weeks while SMH fell 14%, and gains most if MSFT, META and AMZN reaffirm the ~$725B AI spending plan.

It posted the cleanest beat of the season ($7.94 vs $7.20, record $230B backlog, free cash flow back to +$2.9B) and is still 16% below its $692 high; it is sized below RTX after a +14.5% week so defense stays at 32% of the book.

thesis: This is the quarter's densest cluster of make-or-break events: FOMC and MSFT/META on Wednesday, GDP and PCE plus AAPL/AMZN on Thursday, XOM/CVX on Friday. They land on a stagflation-lite tape (10Y 4.70%, WTI $89, VIX 18.7, SMH -14% in four weeks), so the book holds no name that reports this week. It leans on the leadership where beats were actually rewarded and the rotation money is flowing: defense (RTX, LMT), large-cap healthcare (JNJ) and the bank that gains from rising rates (JPM), with NVDA as the one hedge against a short-squeeze tech rebound. Energy and materials stay out under the Council's Rule 1 (DXY 101.43 with the 10Y at 4.70%) and because XLE's RSI is 86. Cash is 15%, well under the Council's 35-45%, because judged against SPY, cash is just a bet that SPY falls, and the evidence for a down week is mixed.
risks: A mild Fed, strong MSFT/META spending guidance and an Iran ceasefire together could set off a short-squeeze rotation back into beaten-down tech and out of defense and defensives, leaving this defensive-tilted book behind SPY; a hyperscaler spending cut would hit NVDA, and a hike or sustained $100 oil would hurt everything except defense. I have no memory of how this week went (my training data ends months earlier) and nothing here uses hindsight; the wikis also contradict each other on earnings dates and some semiconductor prices, so prices.csv was treated as the source of truth.
